items.claim: In the 2025 regular season, Stafford recorded 4,707 passing yards, 46 touchdown passes, eight interceptions, 7.9 yards per attempt, and a 109.2 passer rating.

Stafford led the NFL in 2025 with 4,707 passing yards and 46 touchdown passes; locked control Drake Maye led in passer rating at 113.5 and completion percentage at 72.0%, while Stafford ranked second in passer rating at 109.2.

The 2025 AP MVP vote directly compared locked controls Stafford, Maye, and Allen: Stafford finished first with 366 points, Maye second with 361, and Allen third with 91; locked control Lawrence finished fifth with 49.

limitations: Fresh matched evidence was found for Stafford against Drake Maye, Josh Allen, and Trevor Lawrence, but not a complete common-source comparison packet covering Joe Burrow, Jordan Love, Dak Prescott, Brock Purdy, Justin Herbert, Sam Darnold, Patrick Mahomes, Lamar Jackson, and Jared Goff.
Locked-control full-card attributes remain unavailable, so exact attribute-level comparisons cannot be established.

items.claim: In the 2025 regular season, Matthew Stafford recorded 388 completions on 597 attempts (65.0%), 4,707 passing yards, 46 touchdowns, 8 interceptions, 7.9 yards per attempt, and a 109.2 passer rating in 17 games.

Compared with Patrick Mahomes in the 2025 regular season, Stafford had more passing yards (4,707 to 3,587), touchdowns (46 to 22), yards per attempt (7.9 to 7.2), and a higher passer rating (109.2 to 89.6); Stafford had fewer interceptions (8 to 11), while Mahomes played 14 games.

Compared with Lamar Jackson in the 2025 regular season, Stafford had more passing yards (4,707 to 2,549), touchdowns (46 to 21), a higher completion percentage (65.0% to 63.6%), and a higher passer rating (109.2 to 103.8); Jackson had higher yards per attempt (8.4 to 7.9), one fewer interception (7 to 8), and played 13 games.

Compared with Jared Goff in the 2025 regular season, Stafford had more passing yards (4,707 to 4,564), touchdowns (46 to 34), and a higher passer rating (109.2 to 105.5); both averaged 7.9 yards per attempt and threw 8 interceptions, while Goff had the higher completion percentage (68.0% to 65.0%). Both played 17 games.

limitations: This micro-batch contains aggregate regular-season passing evidence only; postseason, rushing, play-level, pressure, depth-of-target, accuracy, and film-charting comparisons were not collected.
